Definition: apparently of Latin origin; left-handed; Scevas (i.e. Scævus), an Israelite:--Sceva.
BiblicalUsage: Scevas was a Jew, a chief of the priests, whose seven sons tried to cast out evil spirits by the name of Jesus whom Paul preached. The evil spirit answered that it knew Jesus and knew Paul, but asked who they were, and the possessed man leaped on them and overcame them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Sceva's sons are the warning against borrowing a name you do not know, because the spirits know the difference between faith and imitation.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
